title: The web build starts
summary: Patch 0021 mends the browser version. Its title no longer freezes while shaders compile - they compile under a loading screen that now shows, with its bar, in the browser; the terrain no longer runs the web renderer out of its instance slots (one value a patch on the desktop, none in the browser), and planets' skies, the sea and the vein hologram read the depth buffer the way the web's renderer stores it - the sky is blue again.

steps.title: A title that answers
steps.text: In a browser the title screen froze for about 15 seconds - one to four frames a second - while it compiled every 3D shader in turn, and Start game seemed dead. There the title now only loads in the background; the shaders compile under the loading screen. The title runs at 60 FPS from its first second.

steps.title: A loading screen in the browser
steps.text: On the desktop the game has no loading screen: the world shows as it's made, in a second or two. In a browser it takes about half a minute, and a black screen looked like nothing was happening - there the loading screen and its bar show now.

steps.title: Terrain without instance uniforms
steps.text: The web's renderer gives each instance with instance uniforms 16 of its 4096 slots - 256 instances in all - and a planet's terrain has some 730 patches: 492 errors at every load. There the terrain works out each vertex's place from the planet's transform, set every frame, and finds the carves near it itself; the dug ground is marked in its mesh. On the desktop a patch keeps one value instead of three.

steps.title: The sky back
steps.text: Planets' skies were black in a browser: the atmosphere read the depth buffer in the desktop renderer's range (reversed, 0 to 1), not OpenGL's (-1 to 1), and took the ground to be at your eye. The atmosphere, the sea's underwater pass and the vein hologram now read it the right way for each renderer.

review.intro: The code behind patch 0021: the web build fixed - a title that no longer freezes while shaders compile, a loading screen in the browser, terrain without instance uniforms in the web's renderer, and the depth buffer read in its range (the sky, the sea, the vein hologram).
